title: Level 4 (Expert) - C-21
notes:
West leads the ♥K against 6NT. There are 11 top tricks (the ♠A, the ♥A, 7 diamonds, and 2 clubs). West is marked with the ♠K for his Michael's cue bid. It seems at first glance that West's opening heart lead should be allowed to hold to rectify the count for an eventual squeeze against West.

If West continues hearts, South can win the ♥A, cash the top clubs and run the diamonds. On the play of the last diamond, South can discard a heart and West is squeezed. South's twelfth trick will come from either the ♥10 or ♠Q, depending on West's discard.

West can break up the impending squeeze by switching to a diamond at trick 2. South will have no choice but to run the diamonds. The inability to cash the top clubs and the ♥A will stop the squeeze from functioning.

South should thus win the ♥A at trick 1 and play to strip squeeze West. The top clubs are cashed and the diamonds are run. On the play of the last diamond, South pitches a heart and West has no good answer. Discarding a spade allows South to drop the ♠K. Discarding a heart exposes West to a throw-in. A heart is exited to West, forcing him to lead into South's spade tenace.

This type of squeeze matures with 2 or more losers. In the current hand, West is squeezed out of a surplus winner so that he can be endplayed without being able to cash enough tricks to defeat the contract.
